brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource Team: How to Activate a New Accounting Firm

questions.question: What is the pricing structure for client books on the white-label platform?
choices: $20 for the first book, then $17, $15, $14, and $13 as the firm grows
$25 for the first book, then $20 for all additional books
$15 per book flat rate regardless of quantity
$20 per book with a 10% discount after ten books
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the tiered pricing starts at $20 and decreases as firms add more books.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pricing structure is tiered, not flat or based on discounts. Review Slide 3 for the correct tier rates.

questions.question: When creating a Firm ID in Step 1, what are the naming requirements?
choices: It must be uppercase with spaces, like "Smith Co"
Short, lowercase, with no spaces, such as "smithco"
It can be any format as long as it contains the firm's full legal name
It must include numbers and special characters for security
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—Firm IDs are short, lowercase, with no spaces, and must be chosen carefully because they never change.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Firm ID has specific formatting rules to ensure consistency. It should be short, lowercase, and contain no spaces, as shown in Slide 4.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the License Service in the ESource system?
choices: It stores all client bank statements and transactions
It sends sign-in codes, enforces plan limits, keeps book counts, and distributes encryption keys
It manages the firm's branding and web address
It creates monthly billing invoices automatically
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the License Service handles sign-ins, plan enforcement, book counting, and key distribution while protecting data privacy.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The License Service has a specific set of functions focused on access control and counting, not data storage or billing. Review Slide 2 for its actual role.

questions.question: In Vercel's DNS configuration, what does setting the proxy cloud to gray mean?
choices: It enables Vercel's security certificate and speeds up the connection
It blocks all traffic to the firm's web address
DNS only—an orange cloud would block Vercel's security certificate
It allows the firm to use multiple domains at once
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the gray cloud means DNS only, and it's critical because an orange cloud blocks Vercel's security certificate.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The proxy cloud setting is important for Vercel's security. Gray means DNS only, while orange would cause certificate issues. See Slide 6 for details.

questions.question: What information does the License Service never receive from the system?
choices: Sign-in codes and plan tier information
Client names, bank statements, and transactions
The firm's web address and branding settings
Monthly book usage counts
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the License Service is designed not to see sensitive client data like names, statements, or transactions.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The License Service is intentionally limited in what it can access to protect client privacy. Review Slide 2 to see what it does and does not handle.

questions.question: How is monthly billing determined according to the "Highest by month" system?
choices: Bill the average number of books used per day across the entire month
Bill based on the peak number of client books active on any single day that month, using the firm's tier rates
Bill a flat fee regardless of how many books were used
Bill only for the books added during the month, not those deleted
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—"Highest by month" captures the maximum number of active books on any single day and that determines the bill.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The billing system uses the peak count, not averages or flat fees. This ensures firms are billed fairly based on their actual highest usage. See Slide 9.

questions.question: What should you do before activating a firm if an employee's work laptop is lost or stolen?
choices: Ask the owner to pay a replacement fee before proceeding with activation
Skip the activation until the laptop is recovered
Remove that person's access on the License tab so books remain encrypted and unreadable
Reset all passwords for everyone at the firm immediately
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—removing their access is the correct security response, and the encrypted books on the device remain unreadable.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The proper response to lost or stolen devices is to remove the person's access immediately; encryption protects the data even if the device is compromised. Review Slide 10.

questions.question: What is the most likely reason a user cannot add a new client book?
choices: The firm's browser cache needs to be cleared
They are offline (because adding a client needs internet) or the firm's plan is full
The owner has not yet signed in for the first time
The License Service is down for scheduled maintenance
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the two primary causes are being offline or reaching the firm's book limit, and the latter is an upselling opportunity.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The most common reasons for not being able to add a client are connectivity or hitting the plan limit. This is a useful support insight from Slide 10.

questions.question: Which step must happen before the owner can add staff members to sign in to the firm's account?
choices: The firm must complete its first month of billing
The owner must sign in themselves and access the License tab
ESource must approve each staff member through an email verification
The firm must upgrade to a higher tier plan
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the owner signs in first, then uses the License tab to add each staff member's name and work email.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The owner is the key to adding staff; they sign in first and then manage the team from the License tab. Review Slide 7 for this onboarding sequence.

questions.question: Why is it important to confirm that all four prerequisites are in place before activating a firm?
choices: It ensures the firm pays the highest tier rate
It prevents the License Service from crashing
A signed agreement, agreed plan limit, security plan, and security lead assignment protect legal standing and data security, and prevent billing disputes
It guarantees the firm will have no support questions
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—these four prerequisites cover legal compliance, capacity planning, and security readiness, forming a foundation for smooth activation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The prerequisites exist to protect both ESource and the firm legally and operationally. They ensure clarity on terms, capacity, and security before the firm goes live. See Slide 3.
